_: The update card's changelog. Newest first. Each entry: build (the stamp it shipped as), title, notes. newsSince() shows entries until it meets the running build — keep this list short and honest.

entries.title: The laws, and the one ring
notes: ONE RING, and it travels: the single most useful action on the screen wears a conic-gradient light that genuinely turns — the language your browser leans toward, then the invitation to press play, which it leaves the moment the music starts, because a mark that never goes away is decoration. There is exactly one of it in the document, so the rule that there may only be one cannot be broken by forgetting

the turn is a registered custom property (@property with syntax:"<angle>"), which is the only way a conic gradient can rotate at all — so it runs on the compositor and keeps turning while the main thread draws thirty-six rooms; reduced motion stops it dead and keeps the mark

FITTS'S LAW, without moving a pixel: every control now reaches a real target — 44 px under a thumb, 24 under a mouse — through a transparent layer that grows the TARGET and not the ink, budgeted to half the gap so it can never swallow its neighbour. Where the gap could not pay for it, the gap is what changed; the seek strip and the volume slider grew for real, because a drag has to begin inside the thing being dragged

ten HUD chips are now three groups — the room, comfort and power, the mix — with the air between them beating the air inside one by 2.7×, ordered so that what you came for opens, the booth closes, and the set-once controls sit in the middle where things that are set once belong

the catalog box accepts what people actually paste: a bare hostname, a directory, a link still wearing its quotes or the full stop of the sentence it came from — and upgrades an http link on an https page instead of failing silently on mixed content, while still refusing javascript:, data: and file: rather than guessing

twenty named laws became twenty pure functions with a unit suite, and a new probe (tools/ux_probe.mjs) measures the shipped page against them by hit-testing rather than by reading the stylesheet — it found the scene dots and the top bar quietly keeping their old sizes, and said so

entries.title: The oscilloscope
notes: a new room: SCOPE — one cathode-ray tube with a green P31 phosphor, ruled ten by eight, and a beam that draws: Lissajous figures whose ratio is the interval and whose turn is the beat, the harmonograph's decaying spirals struck by an onset, a wireframe polyhedron in vector-display style, epicycle rosettes whose harmonics are the bands, and a dual-trace Y–T sweep of the live waveform, triggered on a rising edge, over the live spectrum

every segment is lit by the beam's DWELL — slow curves burn, fast retraces vanish — so the blanking between a solid's edges is never coded; the phosphor's persistence lengthens in a calm passage, a TRIG lamp blinks on the onset, and a hand on the glass is the position knob

entries.title: Video game mode
notes: a new room: ARCADE — one cathode-ray tube and six of the games every arcade had, played by the music. A chomper walks a MAZE of pellets with four spooks after it, a fleet of INVADERS marches with its ranks lit by the bands (bass at the bottom, treble at the top), a wall of BRICKS is the live spectrum, a tidy player stacks BLOCKS in a well, a SNAKE hunts its food, and two paddles keep a PONG rally — every move on the half-beat, an onset a shot or a kick, a real kick slamming a block home

the games are drawn on a 256×192 canvas and one shader makes it a television — barrel glass, scanlines, a slot mask, bloom, chromatic fringing on the hit, a bezel, and the light the picture throws on the cabinet — so the room costs one small texture a frame and is never heavy
your hand on the glass is the paddle; CALM and reduced motion cut the flash, the fringing and the shake

entries.title: The rail before the speaker, and the booth grows a second hand
notes: the master now ends in a brickwall TRUE-PEAK LIMITER on the audio thread — three milliseconds of lookahead so the gain has arrived before the peak does, a cubic between the samples so a peak no sample carries is still seen, one gain for both channels so the image never lurches, and bit-exact unity below the ceiling: a clean set never touches it, and the booth's new LIM lamp stays dark to prove it

the volume is never written, it is ramped — a slider drag used to be forty small steps in the waveform — and the analyser's band edges are now frequencies rather than bins, so the visuals dance to the same crossovers on a 48 kHz machine as on a 44.1

HOT CUES: eight per track, remembered on the device, snapped to the beat line when set and QUANTISED when pressed — mid-beat, the jump waits for the line and lands with the phase intact; ⇧1–⇧8 from the keyboard, flags on the waveform in the pad's colour, hold to clear

BEAT JUMP, one to sixteen beats either way (, . < > from the keyboard), moving a held loop with it; a three-band EQ on the mix with KILLS that read as gone and breathe back in without a step; a KEY LOCK pad, so the pitch can ride the tempo like vinyl when that is the cleaner sound; and the waveform is a scrub strip

the seamless loop learned three honesties: it refuses to cut across a tear in its own tape and takes the next lap instead; letting go now ASKS the deck whether it has the bytes and waits with the loop covering rather than handing back into silence; and a route change re-measures the tape on the device that is actually there
and the clock now tells the booth where the beat lines actually are: loops, cues and jumps land on the track's own healed lattice rather than on multiples of the beat from zero
the room changes hands with the music: a seam cues the scene change on the audio clock, landing a beatmix's on the bass swap and sized to it, so the picture and the low end move together

two fingers, two axes: spread them and the room comes closer, pinch and it recedes — the first finger keeps the orbit, the second its force, and a third finger no longer orphans the hand that was holding the field
⇧L cycles the lens and W the touch force — L and F were quietly doing two jobs each and only ever managing the first

entries.title: The room learned to dance
notes: a CHOREOGRAPHER now sits above the beat: instead of reacting frame by frame, the camera is dealt FIGURES that span bars — the carousel, the weightless float, the creep toward the heart, the reveal, the pendulum that leans into its own swing, the sixteen-beat corkscrew, step-turns that land quantised on each beat, the whip that winds up against the turn before tearing through the downbeat — each carried for its counted beats and handed over on the count

musical time itself runs RUBATO: every room's own motion steps through a bent clock, thickening to a crawl in a held breath and surging through the whip — the speeds of the dance, not just its shapes; monotone by construction, so nothing ever rewinds
the dancer keeps choreography's oldest secret: the figure that opens a phrase becomes a motif the next phrase may call back — repetition the body recognises without being told

precognition already saw the drop coming; now the whole rig COILS on it — a held near-stillness, time at a crawl, released in the last bar so the landing arrives at full speed as a crash cut on the exact hit

every figure is pure and measured before it ships: bounded on the rig, continuous at the handover, its rubato clamped where no simulation can break — and reduced motion stands the entire choreographer down
a wall of stage screens breathes as one body: the booth's bent clock rides the wire

entries.title: The medium that spirals, the field that spells, the clip you keep
notes: a new room: EXCITABLE — the Barkley model of excitable media (the equation behind the BZ dish and heart tissue), genuinely integrated on the GPU: nothing draws a spiral, the equation rotates it; every onset is an electrode that births a wave, loudness runs the clock, and your finger draws live fire on the medium — three weathers (spiral, meander, storm), each dealt from the playing track, each parameterisation MEASURED alive by the test suite before it shipped

a second new room: VERSE — nine thousand dots that assemble the song's own words letter by letter, breathe them against the beat with their outlines igniting on the treble, and dissolve them back into weather; drop a .txt on the field and its lines become the verse, drop an image and the dots raise it as a TOTEM, luminance carried dot by dot — every script the packs speak shapes correctly, because the rasteriser is the browser's own

CLIP — press X and the show is being kept: the composited canvas plus exactly what the room hears off the master bus, packed locally, saved to your downloads, sixty seconds max, a red light showing the whole time — nothing ever leaves the machine
LOOKS — press K and this exact moment (scene, lens, colour) is written into the link and copied, validated on the way back in; open the link anywhere and the room walks its dials back
mixsets learned to plan the ROOM: a section may carry a visual cue — {"visual": {"scene": "verse", "lens": "mirrors"}} — and the first dance gets its words the way it gets its song
thirty-five rooms; the auto director still runs the night, and every one of these is a nudge it folds in, never a lock

entries.title: The sky above the storm, and the lamps come along
notes: two more lit transitions: SPRITE — the lightning that happens ABOVE a storm, a slow carmine glow discharge (N₂'s own red) with blue tendrils reaching below it — and ECLIPSE, where totality crosses the room, the corona opens in noise-drawn streamers with the chromosphere's Hα at the rim, and the handover happens in the dark, because that is the one moment nobody can watch a landscape change hands

the RIG RIDES THE TRANSITIONS now: while a lit segue crosses the screen, the DMX lamps lean toward the same physics-derived colour on the same clock — the reactor wall pulls the room blue, the burn pulls it warm, and the eclipse genuinely darkens the rig through totality; the strobe channel is never touched, and a blackout is never woken

three more pages in the creature's book: the SIPHONOPHORE drifts as a colonial chain trailing coiled tentilla, the RADIOLARIAN bristles glass spicules from a golden-angle lattice sphere, and the MOTH beats two dotted wing-fans to the bass, eyespots igniting at the wing edge
nine animals, twelve ways for one room to become another, and every colour still an integral, not an opinion

entries.title: The room changes hands under a wall of light
notes: three lit transitions join the segue vocabulary: CHERENKOV — a wall of the exact blue a reactor pool glows (the 1/λ² spectrum integrated against the eye at boot, not a hex somebody liked) crosses the room, the water dimming around it, charged tracks racing the front
AURORA — the sky's two real lines, oxygen green at 557.7 nm with the N₂⁺ violet climbing above, descend as a curtain whose hem wobbles and whose folds drift
EMBER — no front at all: the old room catches grain by grain, highlights first, the paper browning just ahead of a flame that glows between two real blackbody temperatures
all three keep the house rule: the handover hides on a wide dithered band inside the glow, so there is a wall of light but never a line a ruler could find

the drop still gets its quick forms, a quiet passage may now get the sky, and reduced motion still gets the plain crossfade — a light that crosses a room in half a second is a flash, and the flash stays refused

entries.title: The creature learns the song — six pages, and light that swims
notes: every song now grows ITS OWN animal: the creature's whole deal — page, genome, pose — is seeded from the playing track's identity, so the same song grows the same creature tonight, next month, on anyone's phone

the ribs wear the live spectrum: each station along the body reads its own frequency bin, so bass swells one end, treble shivers the other, and a chord is a posture — the creature IS the song's spectrum with a spine
every onset sends one pulse of light down the body's own coordinate — bioluminescence, not a blink — and the rib field drifts on the π and e clocks, so the animal never strikes the same pose twice

three new pages in the book: the OUROBOROS bends the spine into a ring that eats its own tail, the KELP roots it to the floor and sways, and the COMB JELLY ripples the onset light down cilia rows the way the real animal does
a re-deal on the same page now metamorphoses the living body toward the new genome instead of swapping it, and a held touch is a current the creature's free end leans into — you can lead it by hand
all of it rides signals the app already keeps — the spectrum texture, the π/e phases, the onset clock, the touch metric — so a phone pays for none of it twice

entries.title: Something alive in the water — the organic shape engine
notes: a new room: CREATURE — not biology, just two cosine waves and a rule: one wave swims the spine, the other lays the rib field along it, and where that wave's square clears its threshold the rib tips ignite ember-red

three pages from the same genome, the way a book of shapes turns them: the WYRM lays the field on an open spine, the MEDUSA hangs it from a scalloped blob rim as tentacles, the BLOOM opens it into petals around a golden-angle whorl
every visit deals a fresh genome — rib count, curl, wave amplitudes, ignition threshold — so no two creatures are the same animal

the music is the life in it: bass is breath, treble lights the tips, a hard onset is a startle (the ribs snap out, the bell jets, the whorl flares), and the animal grows in along its own body as the track plays

entries.title: The wall earns its frames — every scene, one picture, seams and all
notes: every scene now spans a wall of televisions as one picture — the fractal, the op-art rooms, the pulse, the parlor and the lava lamp used to draw the whole composition on every screen; each takes its slice of one shared field now, like everything else always did
the lava lamp on three screens is one lamp three screens wide, not three little lamps
SEAMS — the video-wall knob: the field passes behind the televisions' frames instead of teleporting across them, cycled through the sizes real frames come in and remembered for your rig

the Which? card grew the wall trade's alignment ritual: each screen shows its edges, and one ball rolls the whole wall — crossing a seam on time is the proof the cut is right, and with seams on it disappears behind the plastic and comes out the other side when a real ball would
works the same on the wire: sixteen devices wear their frames exactly like sixteen monitors

entries.title: The lava lamp gets its droplets
notes: the wax now breaks into a beaded chain of drops pinching off a rising column, instead of travelling as one lump — the physics was already doing it, the picture just could not show it

a droplet of a few particles is genuinely thinner than the middle of a pool, so any threshold that drew the pool correctly made small drops vanish; dividing each particle by its own density fixes it, and costs nothing because the solver had already measured it
the wax casts a shadow through the fluid above it now — the only light is under the column, and without that the lamp read as a flat cut-out however good the wax looked
nearly twice as many particles for the same money: every pass of the solver wanted the same four numbers about the same pair, and now they are worked out once instead of five times
which also bought a third pass of the incompressibility solver — the wax is three times less squashable and a third calmer than it was yesterday
and a phone is budgeted as a phone from the first frame, rather than after the frame governor has spent ten seconds discovering it

entries.title: Crowd mode — the whole floor, in their hands
notes: type “crowd” into the Stage card and put the QR on the projector: anyone who scans it taps once and their phone becomes the show — the whole field, dancing to the room
each phone listens through its own microphone, so the speakers are the broadcast and it scales to any crowd the room holds — two phones or two thousand cost the booth the same: nothing
the booth sends only a pulse — three colours and a scene, about eighty bytes every couple of seconds — so every phone glows in the booth's palette and changes scene when the booth does
phones need only internet (cellular is fine — they never talk to your laptop); if the booth goes quiet the floor keeps dancing, in colours of its own
this is not the wire: a crowd phone is a hand holding the whole show, not a tile of the wall — and the stage wall itself grew to sixteen screens

entries.title: The catalog now knows what a track is made of
notes: instrumentation: every track carries a bass/percussive/tonal/air fingerprint from a real harmonic/percussive split of its own spectrum — no ML, no tagging by hand

texture: the Crate's mood tooltip now names a track bass-driven, percussive, melodic or atmospheric when it genuinely stands out from the rest of the library — or honestly full-spectrum when nothing does

the song's energy ARC — intro, build, peak, drive, break, outro — is now computed once, server-side, and shipped in the catalog instead of guessed frame-by-frame from whatever of the waveform happens to be loaded

fixed: the visual intensity ceiling silently went flat (always wide open) the moment a track's structure came from the catalog instead of the browser — it now reads the catalog's own section energies instead of an envelope that was never shipped
loop stutter is gone: looping now hands the section to the browser's own audio loop instead of re-triggering it by hand every pass

entries.title: Any device is a screen — four letters, and your iPad joins the stage
notes: type “invite” into the Stage card and you get four letters and a QR — scan it with an iPad, a phone or another laptop and that device is a screen of your stage

no pixels are streamed and nothing is mirrored: each device renders the field on its own GPU from about forty numbers a frame, sent directly between the machines — so there is no casting lag and the visuals sit on the beat
two devices are a row of two; a third walks in and the field re-cuts to thirds, live
a screen that reloads, or loses Wi‑Fi for a minute, rejoins under the same four letters by itself — same screen, same slice, nobody reads a new code aloud
the booth counts them beside its own screens, Identify puts a number on every glass, and closing the stage says goodbye to every device instead of leaving them frozen
the code is the same front door the games at kmay89.com use — the mailbox carries only the handshake, never a frame of the show, and forgets everything in fifteen minutes

entries.title: The stage places its own windows now
notes: in Chrome and Edge, stage mode can put each screen fullscreen on the monitor you name — the trick that used to need the Mac app, now behind one permission prompt on your own click
screens are dealt to monitors as they actually hang: the leftmost television is screen one, even when the system counted them in another order
a stage window that landed on its monitor but not fullscreen fills it on a double-click — and the same double-click works on any stage screen, anywhere
the booth and every room-sized screen now hold the display awake for the length of the set — nothing dims mid-show because nobody touched it for an hour
plugging a monitor in (or losing one) mid-show is announced instead of ignored
Safari and Firefox keep the old manners: windows open in a row, and you drag each onto its television

entries.title: The lava lamp’s wax is now a fluid
notes: the wax used to be a dozen discs that merged when a rule said so — it wobbled, because a disc with a shape has a resonant frequency and wax does not ring, wax creeps

it is a real fluid now: a couple of hundred particles solved for incompressibility, so the wax holds a volume instead of a radius — a pool spreads on the heater and a droplet is round because it has to be, not because anything says so

nothing decides that two blobs have merged any more, because nothing can: surface tension pulls them the last little way, the contact widens on its own, and the neck fills in over about a second. A thread that thins past a point pinches
viscosity is the line that makes it wax: a blob struck by another does not bounce and does not ring, it deforms and then it stops
a big blob has a hot skin and a cold core, because heat gets in the same way drag does — through the surface — and that is the whole mechanism behind the plume that lifts off the pool
and it is cheaper than the old one: the surface is splatted rather than tested against every pixel, so the number of particles no longer costs anything to draw

entries.title: A lava lamp that is simulated, not animated
notes: a new room — THE LAVA LAMP: wax that rises because it is warm, thins because it is hot, tears apart when it is going too fast, and rings like a struck drop for a second after two blobs collapse into one

the pool at the bottom is stuck to the heater by its own wetting film and pays out droplets from underneath — and on the rare occasion it warms enough to let go, it comes apart into a rising column of droplets on the way up, which nobody scripted

real refraction through the surface, split into three wavelengths, over the coil’s own light in the fluid behind; thin edges pale, fat middles deep, and bubbles that zig-zag on the way up the way rising bubbles actually do
the music is the thermostat: bass and the track’s arc turn the coil up, and everything else — how fast the wax climbs, how readily it breaks — follows from that one number
put a hand on it and the wax flows, and keeps flowing after you let go
a device that cannot afford as many blobs gets fewer, larger ones rather than a coarser picture — which is more like a lava lamp, not less

entries.title: The field can have a screen of its own
notes: stage mode: the visualizer goes fullscreen on a second screen or a TV and this window becomes the booth — hold the fullscreen button, press ⇧F, or tap Stage
the booth folds into a corner player: what is playing, the transport, and a pad that puts your hand on the picture the room can see — the chevron opens the rest
a stage screen carries no controls, no library and no sound of its own; it draws what the booth hears, and says so if the booth goes quiet instead of freezing
several screens draw one field rather than one picture each — screen 2 of 3 shows the middle third of a single camera, so a shape crossing the seam stays one shape
fixed: on the Mac app, CATALOG opened nothing and stalled the audio — every dialog is the app’s own now, so naming a journey and erasing history work there too
the microphone says which of the four things went wrong, and on the Mac it opens the privacy pane where the answer actually lives
the Mac app no longer offers to install the app you are already in
the Mac app’s own update is offered instead of installed behind your back — same card, same three choices, and your place is saved before it restarts

entries.title: "You're up to date" — a status that finally says so
notes: fixed: the update card could still come back reading "→ new" over and over — an announcement from an outdated background worker, or a check made while the site was unreachable, was believed without ever being verified
an offer that cannot name the build it brings is now re-checked against the site on every update check, and withdrawn the moment it turns out to be the build you already run

when a check finds you current while the card is open, the card now says "You're up to date" with the build id — and applying a refresh says the same, so the end of the loop is something you can actually see

entries.title: The update that knew it had landed
notes: fixed: applying an update could leave the app offering you the same one again, over and over, with nothing left to apply — an update you have already applied is now recognised as applied, and the app says so once instead of asking again
the check for a newer version asks the site itself rather than the copy it already has, so "there is an update" is something measured and not something assumed
a background update that carries the version you are running is retired quietly instead of becoming a card — and when there really is a new one, the card names it instead of calling it "new"
the what's-new list is the news you do not have yet: builds that shipped without a note of their own no longer make it repeat the last four

entries.title: The booth grew hands
notes: loops and rolls on eight beat lengths, from a 32nd to sixteen bars — a loop makes the track wait, a roll stalls the music while the track runs on underneath, so letting go lands you where you would have been
a loop latches on the last beat line you actually heard, and halving or doubling it never moves where it began
filter, echo, gate and drive on one knob, every time constant read from the same beat clock the visuals follow — plus a brake that is a turntable losing power, not a fade
AUTO gives the same hands to the room: the echo blooms into a hand-off and the filter opens across a build, chosen from the song's own shape and never during a quiet passage
the moment you touch anything, AUTO steps back and stays back until you arm it again — it will not undo what you just set
fixed: the gate could silently stop on a busy frame instead of chopping
fixed: the booth could knock a blend off its beat lock by resetting a deck's speed just as the mix began

entries.title: The update that kept asking
notes: fixed: the app could offer you an update to the version you were already running, and keep offering it after you applied it
an update is only offered now when the build on the server is genuinely different from the one you have
when a check turns out to be a false alarm, the badge clears itself instead of waiting for a reload

entries.title: No more silence between tracks on iPhone
notes: the next track is now fetched while the current one plays, so the hand-off no longer waits on the network — the gap on a phone drops from over two seconds to the time the player itself needs
this works with the lock screen, not around it: playback never leaves the one element iOS trusts with background audio
on a slow or metered connection the app leaves it alone — Data Saver and 2G/3G are respected
touching the visuals now works on every device: weaker phones get a simpler version of the effect instead of none at all

entries.title: Your hand bends the world now
notes: the touch no longer draws anything on top of the visuals — it deforms the space they live in, and everything obeys
the black hole is genuinely dark because light near it stops coming back, and the bright ring around it is real lensing
hold your finger down and the horizon widens; let go and a wavefront leaves your fingertip and travels out
scenes with no particles answer your touch for the first time — the light itself is bent, so every scene reacts
reduced motion keeps the touch alive at a gentler strength instead of switching it off

entries.title: The auto-mix holds its beat lock
notes: the intermittent glitch in the auto mix is fixed — blends stayed in time on an idle machine and drifted up to a quarter beat when the visuals were working hard
the seam is now lined up against where the outgoing track actually is, so a busy frame can no longer cost a blend its timing
the incoming track is given a moment to get rolling before the fader opens, so a blend starts full instead of easing in from nothing
measured under full visual load: beat error down from 114 ms to under 8 ms, and it is now a test that has to keep passing

entries.title: Shorter, tighter blends
notes: auto-mix now blends in 8 beats by default instead of 32 — a punchier mix, and far less room for two decks to drift apart
the crate's match scores now rate the PAIR (key and tempo) rather than rewarding whichever blend was longest
longer blends are still there per pair in the Mix tuner

entries.title: The Update button, fixed — and a log of what the app does
notes: tapping Update always does something now: if another window already applied it, this one reloads instead of going quiet
"Later" is remembered across restarts — the button keeps a count and reminds you once when the time is up
SHOW mode still holds every update; nothing is ever applied out from under a set
new Activity log at the bottom of the Console: updates, what played, what the system decided — kept on this device only

entries.title: Colour that survives the brightest moment
notes: bright scenes no longer wash out to white — overdriven light reads as deeper colour instead
blowing out to white is saved for the drop, where the music has earned it
the palette is now a full gradient, so sweeps stay vivid instead of going grey in the middle
click the three colour dots in the HUD: AUTO · SPECTRUM · DUOTONE

entries.title: Four more skins
notes: Sakura Night, Solstice, Ultramarine, Garnet & Silver — 12 in all
dialogs, the update bar, and the welcome card now follow your skin too

entries.title: Skins + a bulletproof update bar
notes: 8 skins — dress the whole console; your pick stays on this device
the welcome says it plainly: a free jukebox, loaded and ready
updating shows an honest progress bar that never gets stuck
if a swap ever stalls, the player hands itself back — nothing lost

entries.title: Smart self-updating
notes: updates now arrive by themselves — no more clearing site data
the Update button wears a badge and opens this log
choose: now, after this track, or later (6 h)
⚡ SHOW mode is never interrupted by an update

entries.title: The epic touch
notes: hold to charge, release to detonate
sling the vortex and it keeps spinning
tap on the beat — the field answers louder
✦ AUTO: scenes re-tune your touch as they change

entries.title: Echoes — passing thoughts
notes: quotes drift by like clouds in the calm passages
✧ MUSE floats questions you can answer, kept on this device only

entries.title: Power modes
notes: ⚡ SHOW: full density, screen kept awake
⚡ ECO: half the frames, quarter the pixels — battery goes to the music

entries.title: Mobile booth redesign
notes: real platters on mobile, a live monitor between them
